analysis:
Examined the supplied portions of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (base 1019-1657 and head 1-526). The changes visible in the patch are: (1) head lines ~512-519 add a fail-closed rejection of GLM5 image/video requests that need JSON response_format or required/named tool_choice. It calls releaseBox.fire() before throwing, so the model pin is released and nothing leaks. (2) head lines ~985-1002 set nativeReasoningPrefix so GLM output that is withheld is parsed through typed reasoning channels. (3) The head makeEventStream line ranges (1187, 1231-1241, 1300-1302, 1419, 1470, 1490-1493) are small edits. I could only see the base text for that region, not head. In base, the native-consumer cancellation and terminal-drain logic (base 1225-1230, 1247-1251, 1357-1379) fails closed: a cancelled or non-terminal native stream throws instead of fabricating a successful stop. In every path I read, releaseBox.fire() runs before continuation.finish.

No new network, crypto, authorization, or cache-scope surface appears in the visible text. cacheScope is still plumbed through submitTokenized unchanged, and nativeMiMo media still passes cacheEnabled:false. That is consistent with T-041, whose cache-scope and HMAC mitigations are untouched here. The change tightens validation and reasoning-channel separation, so it is not a regression.

Limits on this review: the head text for lines 527-1657 is not supplied, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The head versions of the makeEventStream edits and the withholding logic cannot be checked directly. The semantics of GLM5NextPromptPolicy.withholdsOutput and of the native-lease handoff live in unchanged external files. Integration should confirm that the head forwarding loop still preserves the terminal/release ordering and that GLM withheld reasoning does not leak through the SSE path (T-008, T-007). I saw no concrete defect, so no findings, but the unseen head hunks leave a small residual uncertainty.
